agent_answer.notes: All 20 synthetic corpus papers (S001-S020) study whether retrieval augmentation changes a factual-accuracy metric (answer/fact-level accuracy, or a hallucination/unsupported/invented-fact rate) for a parametric closed-book baseline vs a retrieval-augmented model, stating a conclusion in the abstract and conclusion. Comparing each stated conclusion with the two reported condition values: 18 papers (S001-S004, S006-S019) have a conclusion consistent with their reported numbers; 2 papers (S005, S020) claim retrieval augmentation 'does not make the answers measurably more accurate' while reporting a large accuracy gain for the RAG condition (S005: 40.6% -> 53.8%; S020: 52.3% -> 64.6%), so their conclusion contradicts their results. Small-difference cases (S004 -0.9pp, S010 -5.8pp, S015 +3.6pp, S019 -0.8pp) are reasonably described as 'not measurable / essentially unchanged', so they count as agreeing.
